last_attempts_log.asr_text: You call me mad? No, nervous, perhaps, but perfectly sane. My illness sharpened my senses, especially my hearing. I hear everything in heaven and earth. Listen to my calm voice and judge for yourself. I loved the old man who shared my home. He had never hurt me. I wanted none of his money. But his eye, pale blue, covered by a cloudy film, a vulture's eye. Whenever it turned towards me, my blood went cold. I had to be free of it.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: For seven nights, at midnight, I lifted his latch. You should have seen my patience. I eased the door open so slowly he never stirred, then let one thin ray escape my lantern. The eye was always closed, so I could do nothing, you understand. I hated the eye, not the man. Each morning I kindly asked how he had slept. On the eighth night, I nearly laughed at my cleverness. Then my thumb slipped against the lantern's fastening.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: I stood motionless. For an hour he sat in bed, listening. At last, he groaned softly. Not pain, terror. I knew that sound. I uncovered the lantern. Its narrow beam found the eye, wide open. A low, quick beating reached me, like a watch wrapped in cotton. His heart! Faster it went and louder. What if a neighbor heard? I rushed forward. He shrieked once. I dragged him down and pulled the heavy bed over him. Finally, the beating stopped. I checked his pulse. Nothing. I hid his body beneath three floorboards and fitted them back exactly. Not a mark. You could have searched all night. At four in the morning, three police officers knocked. A neighbor had heard a shriek.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: I welcomed them. A bad dream, I explained. The cry was mine. The old man was away in the country. I showed them every room, then brought chairs into his bedroom. I sat directly above the body. You see how little I feared? They chatted pleasantly. I smiled. Then my head began to ache. A ringing filled my ears. But no, that low quick beating again. I spoke louder. It grew louder too. I paced and scraped my chair across the boards. Still they chatted, still they smiled. Louder, louder. Could you have borne it? They heard, they knew. Their smiles were mocking me. I could bear no more. I did it, I screamed. Tear up the planks. Here, it is the beating of his hideous heart.
